brief.summary: Warning: none of the available tools is a hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator. I had literature search tools only, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio values. Any number like that has to come from an emulator the team installs (BACCO 2011.15018, BCemu 2108.08863, syren-baryon 2506.08783) or from published simulation tables. What the literature says: hydrodynamical simulations (OWLS/cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS 1105.1075 and 2309.06479, Horizon-AGN 1801.08559, IllustrisTNG/CAMELS 2511.10634 and 2301.02231, FLAMINGO 2410.17109) agree that baryons cause a small boost at k < 0.1 h/Mpc. Suppression then starts around k ~ 0.1-0.3 h/Mpc, reaches a minimum of roughly 10-30% at k ~ 5-20 h/Mpc depending on the model, and turns upward at higher k where stars and cooled gas concentrate matter. The physics: AGN feedback (thermal or kinetic/jet energy from black-hole accretion) pushes gas out of groups and clusters (about 10^13-10^14.5 Msun/h) past the virial radius. This lowers the halos' baryon fraction and makes their mass profiles shallower. The suppression therefore tracks halo gas fractions closely, which leads to empirical predictors based on cluster f_gas and f_star (2309.02920, 2509.04552, 2409.05716). For weak lensing: without modelling, feedback biases S8 low on small angular scales. Some papers argue that stronger-than-fiducial nonlinear suppression could partly explain the lensing-CMB S8 tension (2206.11794, 2305.09827, 2403.12967). DES Y3 small-scale analyses (2303.05537, 2206.08591), joint X-ray, tSZ and kSZ fits (2110.02228, 2109.04458) and recent kSZ+X-ray+GGL work (2512.02954) point to feedback that is relatively strong but still uncertain. For Stage IV surveys this is a leading systematic: the suppression needs percent-level modelling up to k ~ 10 h/Mpc or it must be marginalised over.

result.summary:
This direction was only partly achieved. No emulator was available, so no S(k) values were computed, and the S_min, k_min and k(1%) table is incomplete. All quantities are at z=0, and every value below is read from published papers.

1. Emulator check (dead end x-01): no tool can evaluate P_hydro/P_DMO. The input file list and the out/ directory are both empty (tc-...-17, -18). Dispatch is set to local (tc-...-19). run_test_job only draws random normal samples on the local machine (tc-...-20).

2. OWLS AGN, the strong/fiducial reference (van Daalen et al. 2011, arXiv:1104.1174, abstract quote; finding f-001). Suppression is 1% at k~0.3 h/Mpc, so k(1%)~0.3 h/Mpc. S(k=1)~0.90 and S(k=10)~0.70. The minimum is at or beyond k=10 h/Mpc, so no interior k_min appears in the 0.1-10 h/Mpc range. Cooling raises power only at k>~70 h/Mpc.

3. BCemu fitted to X-ray gas fractions (Giri and Schneider, arXiv:2108.08863, abstract quote; Figure 8 right panel identified but not read; finding f-007). k(1%) falls at 0.1-0.4 h/Mpc. The maximum suppression is 20-28% (S_min ~0.72-0.80) at k_min ~7 h/Mpc, 68% CL.

4. FLAMINGO (arXiv:2410.17109, abstract; finding f-002). Lower cluster gas fractions and collimated jets give stronger suppression. The strongest models agree with some WL+external-data analyses but are in strong tension with X-ray gas fractions. No numerical S_min or k_min values were extracted.

5. Comparison with the Giri and Schneider 20-28% bound near k~7 h/Mpc: OWLS-AGN reaches 30% suppression at k~10 h/Mpc, at or just beyond the strong edge of the band. The strong FLAMINGO jet and low-fgas variants lie on the strong side of the X-ray-inferred band.

- No weak-feedback S_min or k_min (for example Horizon-AGN, or a low-Mc BCemu point).
- No S(k=5) values.
- No f_b(M500) values; the SP(k) paper, arXiv:2305.09710, was not read.

result.summary:
Partly done. The physical explanation is in place and rests on cited full-text abstract quotes from 5 papers, stored in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_110039/references.bib. The bracket table is incomplete: the strong end has no full-text quotes yet, and Astrid was not read. No figures were extracted.

Physics established:
(1) Gas ejection: AGN feedback heats gas and pushes it out to large distances, which is needed to match X-ray groups (van Daalen+2019, arXiv:1906.00968). The gas moves from inside r500c to r200m and possibly beyond in haloes with M500c >~ 1e13 Msun/h (van Loon and van Daalen 2023, arXiv:2309.06479).
(2) Halo-mass dependence: for k <~ 3 h/Mpc, group-sized haloes of 1e14+-0.25 Msun/h dominate the power spectrum. At smaller scales the summed lower-mass haloes take over. A lower AGN heating temperature damps the effect at k >~ 4 h/Mpc (2309.06479).
(3) Baryon fraction: the mean baryon fraction in groups alone predicts the z=0 suppression to within 1% for k < 1 h/Mpc. Differences in group baryon fraction explain why simulations disagree (1906.00968). A parameter-free model built on halo baryon fractions is accurate to the percent level down to k ~ 10 h/Mpc (2309.06479).
(4) Cooling: radiative cooling raises the power only for k >~ 70 h/Mpc in OWLS (arXiv:1104.1174). Horizon-AGN shows an enhancement of a factor of a few at scales smaller than k ~ 10 h/Mpc (arXiv:1801.08559).
(5) Cosmology coupling: feedback strength scales with f_b/(Omega_m sigma8)^(1/4), and baryonic plus non-baryonic suppression is larger than the sum of the two (Elbers+2024, arXiv:2403.12967).

Bracket at z=0 (partial):
- Horizon-AGN, weak end: suppression < 15% at k ~ 10 h/Mpc; the authors say its AGN feedback is too weak (1801.08559).
- OWLS AGN, intermediate: about 1% at k ~ 0.3, 10% at k ~ 1 (S(k=1) ~ 0.90) and 30% at k ~ 10 h/Mpc (1104.1174).
- Strong end (FLAMINGO jets, BAHAMAS high-AGN): no S(k=1) or S_min values have been quoted from full text yet.

Board posts: findings f-009 to f-013, and question q-05 listing what remains (Astrid 2605.04176, TNG 2511.10634, FLAMINGO 2410.17109 strong-end numbers).

result.summary: Weak-lensing impact assessment (findings f-003 to f-006 and f-008). (1) Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) model the power as P = P_L + A_mod(P_NL - P_L). Keeping Planck LCDM, KiDS-1000 shear needs A_mod ~ 0.69. The tension is KiDS shear S8 = 0.759+0.024-0.021 and DES Y3 shear S8 = 0.772+0.018-0.017 against Planck S8 = 0.829+-0.012: about 9% (2.4-2.7 sigma) and 7% (2.3-2.6 sigma) low. (2) Preston et al. (arXiv:2305.09827): DES Y3 needs milder suppression than KiDS but still more than the simulations give, and it must reach down to k~0.2 h/Mpc. The DES best-fit A_mod value was not extracted. (3) FLAMINGO (arXiv:2309.07959): even its extreme feedback variants are too weak to remove the tension. Current shear data are only marginally sensitive to baryons, and the slight preference for stronger feedback in the D3A cosmology fades once a lower S8 is adopted. The strongest tension is in tSZ y-y, then shear x tSZ, then shear-shear. (4) DES Y3 WL + ACT kSZ (arXiv:2404.06098): S8 = 0.823+0.019-0.020, with feedback more extreme than most simulations. f_b at M500~1e13 Msun is about 1.4 sigma below X-ray; FLAMINGO, MTNG and FABLE predict f_b 1.5, 3.1 and 1.4 sigma higher at about 4e13 Msun, and BAHAMAS agrees best. (5) KiDS x tSZ (arXiv:2109.04458): the cross-correlation alone prefers strong feedback and is about 2 sigma low; adding shear tightens S8 by 40% and gives feedback consistent with simulations. DES Y3 harmonic space (arXiv:2203.07128): S8 = 0.793+0.038-0.025 at 1.5 sigma, and k_max = 5 h/Mpc leaves S8 essentially unchanged. OWLS-AGN (arXiv:1105.1075): about 40% w0 bias for Euclid if baryons are ignored. Verdict: simulation-calibrated feedback (FLAMINGO) cannot resolve the tension. Resolving it needs A_mod-type suppression reaching k~0.2 h/Mpc, beyond what the simulations give; only the WL+kSZ fit prefers such extreme feedback, and the X-ray gas fractions and FLAMINGO argue against it. Gaps: I did not extract a quoted S8 shift in sigma from ignoring feedback for DES/KiDS, the fractional C_ell change at ell 500-5000, or the numerical suppression at k=0.2-1 h/Mpc implied by A_mod=0.69. Full texts are in runs/261017_110039/*.txt, and no cite() entries were added.

With scale cuts it gives 0.805 ± 0.017, 0.9 sigma below. With Amod and free cosmology it gives 0.831 ± 0.036. So leaving out the suppression lowers S8 by about 0.04, roughly 1 sigma of the Amod fit.

- Fiducial (e_w=0.6, v_kin=6500 km/s, eps_kin=6.1): k(1%)=0.59 h/Mpc, k(5%)=2.11 h/Mpc, S(1)=0.979+/-0.001, S(3.7)=0.901+/-0.004. The curve is still falling at k~3.7. (finding f-023)

Lower cluster gas fractions and collimated jets (instead of thermal winds) strengthen the suppression. Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) model the non-linear power as P = P_L + A_mod(P_NL - P_L). With Planck LCDM fixed, a fit to KiDS-1000 cosmic shear needs A_mod ~ 0.69, which is a suppression stronger than recent hydro simulations give. The tension being addressed is KiDS-1000 shear S8 = 0.759+0.024-0.021 and DES Y3 shear S8 = 0.772+0.018-0.017, against Planck S8 = 0.829+-0.012. That is about 9% (2.4-2.7 sigma) low for KiDS and about 7% (2.3-2.6 sigma) low for DES.

Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) find that DES Y3 cosmic shear needs a milder non-linear suppression than KiDS-1000 to agree with Planck LCDM. It is still more extreme than recent simulations, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. They name non-standard dark matter as an alternative cause. The DES best-fit A_mod value was not read in the sections examined.

FLAMINGO (McCarthy et al., arXiv:2309.07959) compares its full suite, including extreme feedback variants, with cosmic shear, CMB lensing, tSZ and their cross-spectra. It concludes that baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension. Current cosmic shear data are only marginally sensitive to baryon physics. Stronger feedback improves the D3A-cosmology fit to KiDS/DES only slightly, and that preference largely goes away once a lower S8 is adopted. CMB lensing agrees well with Planck LCDM. The strongest tension comes from tSZ y-y, then shear x tSZ, then shear-shear.

Bigwood et al. (arXiv:2404.06098) fit DES Y3 WL + ACT DR5 kSZ with BCEmu baryonification. They get S8 = 0.823+0.019-0.020, higher than WL alone. The fit prefers a mean feedback scenario more extreme than most hydro simulations. At M500 ~ 1e13 Msun the baryon fraction comes out about 1.4 sigma below HSC-XXL X-ray. At M500 ~ 4e13 Msun, FLAMINGO predicts f_b about 1.5 sigma higher, MillenniumTNG about 3.1 sigma higher and FABLE about 1.4 sigma higher; BAHAMAS agrees best. They also state that model flexibility alone can shift S8 and degrade its error.

Literature (BCemu, Giri and Schneider, arXiv:2108.08863, not computed): fitting X-ray group and cluster gas fractions gives a z=0 suppression above the percent level at k=0.1-0.4 h/Mpc (so k(1%) lies at 0.1-0.4 h/Mpc). The maximum suppression is 20-28% (S_min ~0.72-0.80) at k~7 h/Mpc, 68% CL. The OWLS-AGN value of 30% at k=10 h/Mpc sits just beyond the strong edge of this band. The FLAMINGO strongest jet and low-fgas models are stated to be in strong tension with X-ray gas fractions.

findings.claim: van Daalen+2019 (arXiv:1906.00968, 92 OWLS/cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS spectra): the large-scale suppression comes from feedback heating gas and ejecting it to large distances, which is needed to match X-ray groups. An empirical model that uses only the mean baryon fraction in groups predicts the z=0 suppression to within 1% for k<1 h/Mpc, and differences in group baryon fraction explain the disagreement between simulations.

van Loon and van Daalen 2023 (arXiv:2309.06479, cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS): AGN feedback ejects matter from inside r500c to r200m and possibly beyond in haloes with M500c>~1e13 Msun/h. For k<~3 h/Mpc, group-sized haloes (1e14+-0.25 Msun/h) dominate the power spectrum; at smaller scales the summed contribution of lower-mass haloes takes over. A lower AGN heating temperature damps the effect at k>~4 h/Mpc for M500c>=1e13.25. A parameter-free model built on halo baryon fractions reaches percent-level accuracy down to k~10 h/Mpc.

Horizon-AGN (Chisari+2018, arXiv:1801.08559) is the weak end of the bracket: suppression at k~10 h/Mpc is <15% at z=0, with an enhancement of a factor of a few at smaller scales from cooling and star formation. Its redshift evolution over z=0-5 is non-monotonic, and the authors conclude its AGN feedback is probably not strong enough.

Elbers+2024 (FLAMINGO, arXiv:2403.12967): baryonic feedback is coupled to cosmology through f_b/c_v^2 ~ f_b/(Omega_m sigma8)^(1/4), which gives an accurate fitting formula for the suppression. Combined baryonic and non-baryonic suppression (neutrinos, decaying DM) is larger than the sum of its parts.

Verbatim from Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794, Eq. 7): with the cosmology fixed to Planck TTTEEE LCDM, the KiDS-1000 xi_pm fit gives "a mean Amod = 0.69 ± 0.06" with chi2_min = 265.5 for 225 data points. The authors note that this uncertainty is underestimated because it neglects the Planck cosmology error. HMCode2020 with a broad prior instead gives Theta_AGN = 9.17+0.2-0.8, well outside the BAHAMAS-calibrated range 7.6-8.0. The paper states that "the power spectrum suppression required to reconcile the KiDS cosmic shear measurements with the Planck cosmology is more extreme than predicted by most of the hydrodynamic simulations" (Fig. 6). For KiDS, ignoring feedback (HMCode2020 no feedback) gives S8 = 0.755+-0.016, against 0.774+-0.021 for the fiducial Theta_AGN = 7.3-8.3 prior (Table 1): a shift of about 0.02, roughly 1 sigma.

Verbatim from Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827). With a Planck prior and no scale cuts, DES Y3 gives "Amod = 0.858 ± 0.052", which differs from unity by about 2.7 sigma (Eq. 3). KiDS reanalysed with the same Planck prior gives Amod = 0.748 ± 0.072, about 1 sigma above the 0.69 of Paper I (Eq. 5). The naive combination is Amod = 0.820 ± 0.042 for DES Y3 + KiDS, meaning suppression is required at about 4 sigma (Eq. 6). Over k <~ 1 h/Mpc, BAHAMAS log10(dT_heat/K) = 8.0 "is well approximated by Amod = 0.9". The required suppression is stronger than that, closer to C-OWLS 8.5/8.7, and must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc (Fig. 2 right, Fig. 6). On S8 when baryons are ignored: DES Y3 with no scale cuts and no feedback (variant 4) gives S8 = 0.793 ± 0.012, which is 1.8 sigma below Planck TTTEEE 0.828 ± 0.016. With scale cuts (variant 3) it gives 0.805 ± 0.017, 0.9 sigma below. Adding Amod with free cosmology (variant 5) gives 0.831 ± 0.036 (Table 2). Removing the baryon-feedback mitigation therefore lowers DES S8 by about 0.04 relative to the Amod-free fit, which is about 1 sigma of that fit.

An analytic stand-in may still be possible: the SP(k) or van Daalen+2019 fitting formulae evaluated by hand from published coefficients. That route has not been tried.

The evidence excerpts show only the first few hundred characters of 10,000-16,000 character text chunks. None of the quoted claim strings is actually visible in the excerpts: the Amod = 0.69 +- 0.06 quote, the 21-28% band, the FLAMINGO 'closely resemble' sentence and the Astrid 'rises back to above unity' sentence. I accepted these findings because the chunk ranges plausibly cover the cited sections (abstracts at chars 0-4000, Sec. 4 later in the text) and the quotes are internally consistent with earlier findings. Future findings should store the exact matching snippet as the excerpt.

issues.text: unsupported: a CRK-HACC hydro emulator (served by `serve-hydro.sh`) was connected — No script or service named `serve-hydro.sh` appears anywhere in the board, directions, findings or dead ends. The board establishes only that a HACC hydro emulator was connected and lists 'Pk-ratio' among its observables (d-07).

unsupported: unity on large scales, with only a sub-1e-4 boost at the weak point — This contradicts the report's own Results section and critique c-06. Both give the weak-point value S = 1.00014 at k = 0.086 h/Mpc, which is a boost of about 1.4e-4, not below 1e-4. Within 1e-4 of unity is claimed only for the fiducial and strong points.

unsupported: Two FLAMINGO results, recorded with validated quotes, frame this: ... arXiv:2309.06479 identifies "group-sized haloes" — The board identifies arXiv:2309.06479 as a cosmo-OWLS/BAHAMAS study of massive haloes, not a FLAMINGO paper. The quote itself is validated (f-025), but its attribution to FLAMINGO is wrong.

unsupported: FLAMINGO (arXiv:2410.17109, arXiv:2306.04024) — The report says this list is what the survey brief summarised. The brief's FLAMINGO citation for the response picture is 2410.17109 only. 2306.04024 appears only in the key-paper list, as the description of the simulation suite.

unsupported: about 0 at k = 0.2 h/Mpc — No S(k = 0.2) value was extracted for any HACC point. The board gives values only for k < 0.09 (within 1e-4 of unity) and the 1% crossing at about 0.5-0.6 h/Mpc. The value at k = 0.2 is an inference and should be stated as below 1% rather than presented as read.
